question: Who Owns Starbucks?
quick_answer: Starbucks is an independent, publicly traded company listed on the NASDAQ under the ticker SBUX, so it is owned by its shareholders rather than a parent company. It was founded in 1971 in Seattle, Washington, and grew into the world's largest coffeehouse chain. Howard Schultz, who built the modern Starbucks, is closely linked to the brand but is not its sole owner.
key_facts: Publicly traded on the NASDAQ under ticker SBUX
Owned by its shareholders, no single parent company
Howard Schultz drove its global growth but does not solely own it

body.heading: Who owns Starbucks?
body.text: Starbucks is a public company, which means it is owned collectively by its shareholders. It trades on the NASDAQ stock exchange under the ticker SBUX and is run by its own management team and board of directors, not owned by a larger food conglomerate.

body.heading: The Howard Schultz connection
body.text: Starbucks was founded in 1971 in Seattle, Washington. Howard Schultz joined later, bought the company in the late 1980s, and transformed it into the global coffeehouse brand it is today, serving multiple times as CEO. While his name is tied to Starbucks, as a public company it is owned by shareholders rather than by Schultz alone.

body.heading: A global public company
body.text: Today Starbucks operates thousands of stores worldwide and remains an independent public company. Anyone can buy shares in it on the stock market, which is what 'owning' Starbucks means in practice.

faqs.a: Yes. Starbucks trades on the NASDAQ under the ticker SBUX, so it is owned by its shareholders.
Not outright. Schultz bought and built the modern Starbucks and led it as CEO, but as a public company it is owned by its shareholders.
